summary: NovaExchange - failover throttle during cross-region surge causing streaming retries and client-visible stalls
description:
Issue summary:
During a customer-triggered traffic surge on 2026-03-12, NovaExchange observed repeated streaming response retries, increased client-side stalls, and a spike in 502/503 errors after automatic failover to eu-west-1. The platform attempted failover routing and activated a throttle policy on the failover pool which caused head-of-line blocking for streaming sessions.

Impact:
- ~12% of NovaExchange requests saw streaming disconnects or repeated partial responses between 2026-03-12 03:22 - 03:58 UTC.
- Customer reported increased API errors and visible delays for order-book features dependent on low-latency streaming.
- Business impact: degraded trading UX for a subset of enterprise customers.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east-1 primary, eu-west-1 failover).
- Affected model types: long-context chat/generation and embeddings.
- Redwood platform version: inference-runtime v2.7.4 + routing service v1.12.

Steps to reproduce (high-level):
1) Simulate cross-region failover by increasing sustained connection count from a single customer pool in us-east-1 while disabling autoscale on dedicated pool.
2) Observe routing decision to eu-west-1 and activation of throttle policy due to configured concurrency ceilings.
3) Streaming clients receive partial events with multiple reconnect attempts.

Logs and artifacts:
- Metrics dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/streaming-slo?orgId=1&from=2026-03-12T03:00:00Z&to=2026-03-12T04:00:00Z
- Error samples attached in comments (support-log excerpts).
- Related incident: INC-20260312-07
comments: 2026-03-12 03:28 UTC - Aisha Khan (Support): Initial triage - customer reported repeated streaming disconnects and 502s after they hit a traffic spike. Escalated to SRE. Link to customer support thread: slack:#support-novaexchange

2026-03-12 03:35 UTC - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Observed traffic redistribution to eu-west-1. Concurrency-based throttle rule triggered on failover pool (policy: failover_concurrency_ceiling_v1). Temporarily increased pool concurrency to reduce immediate impact. Noted head-of-line blocking in streaming worker queue.
2026-03-12 04:05 UTC - NovaExchange (Customer): Confirmed reduced disconnects after throttle bump but still experiencing intermittent partial events. Asked for status update and ETA.

2026-03-12 06:12 UTC - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Applied temporary routing bypass for NovaExchange to route new sessions to a dedicated burst-capacity pool; monitoring for errors. Opened linked internal ticket INT-4132 to investigate routing policy interaction.
investigation_notes: 03:30 UTC - Hypothesis 1: Failover routing combined with an aggressive per-pool concurrency ceiling caused the routing layer to enqueue streaming requests; continuous batching logic prioritized head-of-line large requests, starving new streaming frames (observed via worker queue length metric).

03:40 UTC - Hypothesis 2: KV cache cold starts for long-context models in eu-west-1 increased per-request latency, pushing requests past the throttle window and triggering retries. Check cache-miss rate: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/cache/cache-metrics?from=2026-03-12T02:50:00Z&to=2026-03-12T04:10:00Z

Data points collected: 1) worker_queue_depth increased from baseline 8 -> 220 in eu-west-1; 2) avg per-token latency for redwood/gpt4o-instruct-8k rose from 12ms -> 110ms during event; 3) throttle rule 'failover_concurrency_ceiling_v1' fired 47 times between 03:22-03:40 UTC.
Logs: extracted 30 sample request traces showing repeated 502 returned by routing service before client retries; attached in Confluence page.
Related PR for routing logic change under review: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2871 - introduces queue-aware throttle bypass for high-priority enterprise customers.

Temporary mitigations taken: increased the concurrency ceiling for NovaExchange's failover pool, enabled routing bypass to burst pool, and restarted a small subset of streaming workers to clear backlog. Immediate reduction in customer errors noted (502 rate fell to baseline in ~18 minutes).
resolution: Workaround (applied 2026-03-12 03:40 UTC): 1) Raised per-customer concurrency ceiling on failover pool for NovaExchange. 2) Applied routing bypass to send new streaming sessions to dedicated burst-capacity pool. 3) Restarted 4 streaming workers in eu-west-1 to drain queued requests. These reduced visible customer impact within 20 minutes.

Root cause (preliminary): Interaction between automatic failover routing and an aggressive pool-level concurrency throttle that did not account for streaming session queue dynamics, combined with KV cache cold penalties for long-context models in the failover region. This produced head-of-line blocking and client-visible stalls.

Permanent fix plan (tracked in INT-4132 and PR 2871): 1) Implement queue-aware throttle bypass for high-priority customers (PR under review). 2) Adjust default failover concurrency policy to account for streaming workloads. 3) Add pre-warm KV-cache step for failover model variants. 4) Add synthetic failover load tests to CI and update runbook.

Post-incident actions: 1) Prepare and share postmortem with NovaExchange (owner: Marco Ruiz) by 2026-03-16. 2) Offer one-week service credit per the enterprise contract to NovaExchange (customer success to propose). 3) Add an observability alert for worker_queue_depth > 100 across failover pools. 4) Schedule a cross-team review (SRE + Platform + Product) to update routing/scale defaults.
Status: In Progress - permanent fixes assigned; PR 2871 in review; follow-up runbook update pending.
